statement: For the five-vertex tree T* with edge set {ca, cb, cd, de}, using ordinary (not induced) subgraph comparability on every induced five-vertex subset exactly as frozen in source.md and problem.md, f(T*) = 8. Specifically, 2 K_4 is T*-exact, no nine-vertex T*-exact graph exists, and heredity excludes all larger orders.
contribution: This resolves the frozen single-tree case. The cited source supplies the prior bounds 8 <= f(T*) <= 16 and the lower-bound mechanism; the new contribution is the nine-vertex nonexistence theorem, represented by a complete deterministic 36-variable, 95,382-clause CNF and a full DRUP refutation whose 3,993 additions and 997 deletions were replayed by a separate no-SAT-library checker. A bounded current primary-source search found no later equivalent resolution, but no priority claim is made.
